version.changelog: 1.2.2: single source of truth for the version (CLI reported 0.1.0-mvp while pyproject said 1.2.1); tests/test_version.py fails the build on drift; suite 76 tests

llm.summary: This is a local CloudArc benchmarking workflow with disclosed repository edits and benchmark runs, and I found no hidden credential, network, persistence, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The manual benchmark can consume hours and tens of GiB of temporary disk, but this is disclosed and gated by an explicit --yes flag; smoke/selfcheck paths are bounded.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is described as cloning or installing from the registry; I found no install-time script, dependency bootstrap, remote payload retrieval, or automatic execution path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks an agent to inspect and modify repository files and run test/benchmark commands, but it scopes that work to CloudArc benchmark, protocol, documentation, and workflow files and explicitly says not to use credentials, cloud services, proprietary packages, or make commits without request.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence, memory writing, service installation, scheduled tasks, credential stores, or privilege escalation were present; any lasting effects are user-directed repository artifact changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is bounded-memory CloudArc benchmark and telemetry validation; its file reads, benchmark commands, report generation, and CI/document updates align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only for CloudArc benchmark and telemetry work. Expect it to run local tests and benchmarks and to create or update benchmark reports, docs, and workflow files in the repository. Avoid real cloud credentials as the skill itself instructs, and use the manual benchmark only when you are prepared for large temporary disk and time consumption.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The broad repository read/write and shell-command guidance is part of the benchmark workflow; lack of a separate permission declaration is a packaging note, not evidence of hidden or purpose-mismatched authority.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited text tells the agent to check skipped file counts before treating a pack as complete; it does not instruct autonomous high-impact action.
[AST4] expected: The helper uses subprocess.run with explicit argument lists and shell=False by default to run fixed test and benchmark entry points; this is expected for a local benchmark helper.
[TT2] unexpected: The badge command renders SVG from a benchmark result object using constants and numeric fields, then writes only to the user-specified output path; the claimed stdin-to-file SVG flow is not supported by the inspected code path.
[SQP-2] expected: The badge subcommand intentionally writes an SVG to --output and prints the target path; users should choose output paths carefully, but this behavior is disclosed and purpose-aligned.
